name: Dr. Joannie Marlene Bewa
title: Founder of Global Health and International Development Program
bio:
Dr. Joannie Marlene Bewa is a multi-award-winning medical doctor, influential leader and scientist specialized in public health and women's health. She is a researcher at the University of South Florida College of Public Health (USA) and founded the Young Beninese Leaders Association (YBLA), a non-profit organization addressing health and gender equality in Africa since 2010. YBLA reached over 20 000 adolescents and youth on sexual and reproductive health, HIV prevention and leadership and was awarded the very competitive First lady Michelle Obama Young African Women Leaders Grant. She serves as an advisory Board Member for Merck for Mothers, a 500 USD million commitment to improve maternal health worldwide. During the pandemic, she has established a novel program: the Global Health and International Development Fellowship.

As a woman in science and entrepreneur, Dr Bewa has consulted for the United Nations, Oxfam, the African Development Bank, HIV AIDS Young Leaders Fund, One World UK. She joined the World Health Organization (WHO) technical advisory group as an expert advising the WHO Afro director on RMNACH IN 47 African countries. In 2021, she was awarded two research grants focused on women's access to contraception during the pandemic.

Dr Bewa shared her work in high level spaces including the United Nations, the Canadian parliament in 2017, the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation Goalkeepers forum 2018, and the French Government national humanitarian forum in 2020. Her global impact was acknowledged by governments, the African Union, ONE Campaign, the U.S State Department and the Secretary Clinton Women in Public Service Project.

name: Dr. Alaa Murabit
title: UN SDG Global Advocate, Gates Foundation Director: Health (PAC)
bio:
Dr. Alaa Murabit a medical doctor, global health and security expert and strategist, women's rights advocate, and United Nations High-Level Commissioner on Health Employment and Economic Growth. Alaa is one of 17 Sustainable Development Goal Advocates appointed by the UN Secretary-General due to her leadership on establishing and advancing the SDGs, and a 2020–2021 Fellow at the Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University. She leads The Gates Foundation's Global Policy and Advocacy Health work, in partnership with the Global Health and Global Development divisions. Her work has shaped policies in over 190 countries and impacted the lives of billions.

Alaa founded the women's rights organization Voice of Libyan Women in 2011, at the age of 21. Her TED Talk, “What My Religion Really Says About Women,” has been viewed nearly 7 million times. In 2016, she became executive director of Phase Minus 1, providing thought leadership in conflict resolution and inclusive security, and she later founded CO-AGENCY, an accelerator for emerging women's leadership in security, health, peacebuilding, and policy. A Nobel prize nominee, Alaa is the recipient of more than 100 honors and awards, including the Canadian Meritorious Service Cross, BBC 100 Women, Forbes 30 Under 30, CNN Leaders You Should Know, Nelson Mandela International Changemaker Award, and Harvard Law's Women Inspiring Change. She is an MIT Media Lab Director's Fellow and an Ashoka Fellow, and serves on the board of the Malala Fund. Alaa received an M.D. from the University of Zawia in Libya and an MSc in International Strategy and Diplomacy, with Distinction, from the London School of Economics and Political Science.

name: Zahra Al-harazi
title: Co-Founder at Skillit, Chatelaine Woman Entrepreneur of the Year
bio:
Zahra is Co-founder of Skillit, an experiential marketplace for skills. She also is a consultant with some of Canada's largest companies on Organizational Purpose and Shared Values. Prior to Skillit, Zahra was the CEO and founder of Foundry Communications, a multiple international award winning marketing and communications studio. Foundry was recognize by Profit magazine and one of the most profitable companies in Canada on its W100 list.

She is one of Canada's most powerful women - WXN, Canadian Woman Entrepreneur of the Year - Chatelaine, Calgary's Top 40 Under 40, Business in Calgary's "Leader of Tomorrow" and has received the Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee medal for contributions to Canada and the RBC Top 25 Immigrants to Canada Award.

She is an internationally acclaimed speaker, represented by Speaker's Spotlight and has had the privilege to speak across the globe in countries such as Australia, New Zealand, India, Pakistan, Germany, UK, US, Chile among many others. Her first book, "What It Takes", was published by Harper Collins in Jan. 2020.

Zahra the former Chair of the Fund Development Committee for the Werklund School of Education at the University of Calgary, The Walrus Board, the EO Global Communications Committee, Toronto Board for Entrepreneurs Organization as the Finance Chair, the The OGM Editorial Advisory Board, Global Transportation Hub board and the National Make-a-Wish Foundation Board. In addition, she served as the Canadian Ambassador to UNICEF for four years.

name: Cecilia Aragon
title: Award-Winning Author and Professor at the University of Washington
bio:
Cecilia Aragon is an award-winning author and engineering professor at the University of Washington.

Dr. Cecilia Aragon has worked with Nobel Prize winners, taught astronauts to fly and created musical simulations of the universe with rock stars. Her major awards for research, and a stint at NASA designing software for Mars missions, led President Obama to call her "one of the top scientists and engineers" in the United States. In 2016, Aragon became the first Latina to be named to the rank of Full Professor in the College of Engineering at UW in its hundred-year history.

Her memoir, Flying Free (2020), shares her own journey of breaking past her own fears to become a champion aerobatic pilot. Her first book, Writers in the Secret Garden (2019), takes a close look at the fascinating world of fanfiction to explore how young people express themselves. Her newest book, Human-Centered Data Science: An Introduction, will be released by MIT Press in 2022.
